definition: Open WebUI is a self-hosted graphical user interface for interacting with artificial intelligence models, particularly large language models.
details: It can be used as a browser-based interface for locally hosted models through software such as Ollama and for remote models provided through OpenAI-compatible application programming interfaces (APIs). When used with locally hosted models, Open WebUI can operate entirely offline, while remotely hosted models can be accessed over the Internet through third-party providers. It provides a ChatGPT-style interface while allowing users to select among different models and providers.

explainer.lead: Open WebUI is a self-hosted graphical interface for interacting with AI models, particularly large language models. It matters because it gives a ChatGPT-style front end while letting users choose among models and providers.

tiers.eli5: It's your own private chat window for AI models, running on your computer or a server you control.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers run it against locally hosted models via software such as Ollama, or against remote models through OpenAI-compatible APIs, switching between them in one interface. Pitfall: it is an interface, so model quality and behaviour depend entirely on the backend it points at.
tiers.paperLevel: A self-hosted graphical user interface for AI models, usable as a browser-based interface for locally hosted models through software such as Ollama and for remote models through OpenAI-compatible APIs; with local models it can operate entirely offline.

explainer.example: A user runs Ollama locally, points Open WebUI at it, and chats offline through a ChatGPT-style interface.
